_comment: Data for the generate-midi skill. THREE tables: era profiles (hardware constraints + character), the voice catalog (named instruments mapped to both a General-MIDI program for portable .mid playback AND a chip-synth timbre for the built-in renderer), and form presets (composition briefs with sensible era/tempo/length/loop defaults). Edited by humans/Claude, read by midi.py. See SKILL.md and references/.

nes.label: NES / Famicom (2A03)
nes.character: Five hardware channels but realistically 4 melodic: two pulse waves (duty 12.5/25/50), one triangle (bass, fixed volume), one noise (percussion). No real chords — imply harmony with fast arpeggios on a single pulse channel. Bright, brittle, iconic.

gb.label: Game Boy (DMG) — R/B/Y era
gb.character: Four channels: two pulse, one 4-bit wavetable (the 'wave' — often a soft bass or hollow lead), one noise. Mono. The classic monster-collector handheld sound: thin, catchy, relentless hooks that survive a tiny speaker.

gbc.label: Game Boy Color — G/S/C era
gbc.character: Same 4 channels as DMG, but late-era composers pushed them harder: tighter arpeggios, busier basslines, more confident melodies. The peak of the 4-channel handheld craft.

snes.label: SNES / Super Famicom (SPC700)
snes.character: Eight sample-based voices with per-voice ADSR and a hardware echo unit. Real chords, lush pads, plucked basses, faux-orchestral colour. The platform-action and grand-RPG sound — warm, reverberant, cinematic within 8 notes.

gba.label: Game Boy Advance
gba.character: Legacy PSG channels plus two PCM 'direct sound' channels; most games ran a sampled, MIDI-like sequencer. Brighter and thinner than SNES but more voices than the handhelds before it.

hifi.label: Hi-fi sequenced MIDI (PS1 / GM, FF-VII-era)
hifi.character: Full General-MIDI-style sequencing with a large voice budget and sample-based instruments. The early-3D-RPG sound: ambitious, emotional, orchestral-leaning — 'it's MIDI but it sets the whole scene'.

pulse12.desc: Thin nasal pulse (12.5% duty). Sparkly secondary lead / arpeggio.

pulse25.desc: Classic chip lead (25% duty). The default melody voice.

pulse50.desc: Full square (50% duty). Round, hollow, organ-like.

tri_bass.desc: Triangle in the bass register. The NES/GB low end.

wave.desc: Game Boy 4-bit wavetable — hollow, mellow; bass or pad.

saw.desc: Bright buzzy saw. Aggressive lead / synth brass.

pluck.desc: Short decaying pluck — harp / guitar / koto feel.

bell.desc: Glassy bell / music-box. Sparkle and accents.

strings.desc: Bowed string ensemble (sustained pad with vibrato).

drums.desc: Percussion track. Note names map to kit pieces — see SKILL.md.

drum_map._comment: Note name -> drum sound for the built-in synth. Also written as GM percussion note numbers in the .mid (channel 10).

title.label: Title screen theme
title.use_for: Main menu / boot. The promise of the adventure.
title.form: Short rubato intro -> grand statement of the main motif -> loop body. The single most-heard melody in the game; make the hook unmistakable.
title.voicing: Lead = strings or brass over pad; pluck/bell sparkle; bass + drums optional and restrained.

overworld.label: Overworld / route theme
overworld.use_for: Walking routes between towns; the default exploration loop.
overworld.form: AABA or ABAC, 16–32 bars. Bright, forward-moving, endlessly hummable — it must not annoy after the 20th loop.
overworld.voicing: pulse25 lead, pulse12 harmony/arps, tri_bass walking bass, noise/drums light backbeat.

town.label: Town / village theme
town.form: Relaxed AB, warm major key. Cosy and slightly slower than the road.
town.voicing: pulse25 or wave lead, gentle pulse50 chords-by-arp, soft tri_bass, minimal percussion.

battle.label: Wild encounter battle
battle.form: Driving intro stab -> tense loop. Urgent but exciting, not scary.
battle.voicing: pulse25 lead, pulse12 fast arps for harmony, busy tri_bass, steady noise drums.

boss.label: Boss / rival / champion battle
boss.form: Heroic minor key, bold motif, a clear B-section that lifts. High stakes.
boss.voicing: brass/saw lead, string pad, pluck/arp tension, strong bass + full drums.

cave.label: Cave / dungeon theme
cave.form: Sparse, modal/minor, lots of space. Tension + wonder, slow reveal.
cave.voicing: wave or pulse50 lead with long notes, deep tri_bass, occasional noise drips.

emotional.label: Emotional / story moment
emotional.form: Slow, lyrical, bittersweet. Let one melody breathe over gentle harmony.
emotional.voicing: flute or strings lead, pad, pluck arpeggios, soft bass, no drums.

victory.label: Victory fanfare
victory.use_for: Post-battle win. ONE-SHOT jingle, not a loop.
victory.form: Ascending triumphant phrase that resolves hard on the tonic. 2–6 s.
victory.voicing: brass/square lead + pluck + bass; a crash to finish.

level_up.label: Level-up / learn jingle
level_up.use_for: A creature levels up or learns a move. ONE-SHOT.
level_up.form: Tiny rising 3–5 note flourish. <2 s. Optimistic.

item_get.label: Item-get jingle
item_get.use_for: Picking up a key item. ONE-SHOT.
item_get.voicing: pulse25 + pulse12 harmony, resolve on tonic.

evolution.label: Evolution / transformation theme
evolution.use_for: A creature evolves. Short, can loop briefly during the animation.
evolution.form: Mysterious build with rising tension, then release. Loops until the animation ends.
evolution.voicing: pad + bell shimmer, rising pluck arps, swelling strings.

game_over.label: Game-over / faint theme
game_over.form: Descending, deflating cadence to a minor resolution. 3–6 s.
game_over.voicing: strings or wave lead, low bass, no drums.
